confidence_notes: I used two web searches: one for the latest RBA AUD/USD rate and one for Darwin prices. The searches found 2026 cost-of-living figures from Citycost (updated October 2026), MyLifeElsewhere and Expatistan. I took food, coffee and beer anchors from those figures, rounded to typical values and converted at about 0.672 USD per AUD. Coffee is about A$5.75 and an inexpensive meal is about A$33–36; both are fairly consistent across sources. The mid-range meal for two is about A$125–135. Beer varies a lot: A$9, A$10.54 and A$14.65 per 0.5 L, so I used about A$11. I did not find direct cocktail or wine prices. I based them on the beer price and typical Australian bar ratios, at about A$22 for a cocktail and A$13 for a glass of wine. Accommodation is a general-knowledge model estimate and was not searched. It reflects July 2026, which is Darwin's dry season and peak tourist time, so rooms are probably near seasonal highs. Accommodation is the least certain part. The latest FX rate (November 2026) is later than the July 2026 pricing window.
comparable_city_reasoning: Darwin is a remote Australian capital where restaurant prices are about 17% above the national average. Hospitality and accommodation prices are similar to Cairns or Perth, with higher dry-season rates.
